title: Conditional mutual information under injective recoding of the second and conditioning variables
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a sample space $\Omega$, and let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be measurable random variables on $\Omega$, taking values in countable measurable spaces $S$, $T$, $U$ respectively and each having finite range. Let $f\colon T\to V$ and $g\colon U\to W$ be measurable injections into countable measurable spaces. Then relabelling the second and conditioning variables by $f$ and $g$ leaves the conditional mutual information unchanged:
\[
  I[X : f\circ Y \mid g\circ Z ; \mu] \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z ; \mu].
\]
hypotheses_covered: X, Y, Z measurable random variables into countable spaces
X, Y, Z have finite range
replaced:

  I[X : f \circ Y \mid g \circ Z;\mu] \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
